ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$4.19 to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7) and record the driver's unexplained deviation from the shortest and most direct route under RD-1; no account flag (RD-6 not met).
ruling.reasoning:
Route deviation on a metered (RydeTAXI) trip: the record shows one off-route segment, 12:25–12:36, 4.57 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.60 km, adding 2.97 km [F4], and trip distance 19.0 km against a 15.5 km optimal route [F1]. Under RD-1 each off-route segment is examined under RD-3 / RD-4 / RD-5, and any segment not excused is an unexcused deviation [RD-1].

RD-4 does not excuse it: the trace marks ✗ RD-4(a) — there is no incident on the replaced stretch [F15], and speed-band records alone do not exempt [F13][F14] under RD-4(b)/(c) [RD-4].

The rider's message does excuse the segment: at 12:21, before the segment began at 12:25, the rider named a specific place — "Can you stop at Paya Lebar Square? I need to grab a parcel, 3-4 minutes." [F9] — and the driver accepted ("Ok can") [F10]. The car stopped there (4 min 0 s stationary at a point that is neither pickup nor drop-off) [F2], and the driver confirms the stop [F12]. Under RD-3(a) a rider who names the place makes it the destination, so the whole way driven to reach it is not a detour and its extra km are exempt in full — how long the stop lasted and how far the place was do not reduce the exemption [RD-3].

The exempt segment is not, however, the whole 3.5 km of excess [F1]. The fare record bills $4.91 of excess distance (3.48 km × $1.4100/km) [F5], while the segment's exempt extra km are 2.97 km [F4] — the remainder, about 0.51 km, is mileage outside any measured off-route segment, which RD-2 leaves with the driver [RD-2]. The correct refund is therefore the non-exempt portion of the billed excess: 3.48 km − 2.97 km = 0.51 km; 0.51 km × $1.4100/km = $0.72. Read the other way — the trace's own allowed formula, Σ extra_km of non-exempt segments × $1.4100/km — the non-exempt figure is the same $0.72. I record the driver's unexplained +22% distance against RD-1's shortest-and-most-direct obligation [F1][RD-1].

The waiting amount billed, $1.15 (4.4 min × $0.26/min) [F6], is a metered waiting unit on a RydeTAXI trip and is chargeable per RD-3(c); it is not refunded [RD-3]. Non-metered fare rules (FARE-1) do not apply because this is a metered taxi trip [F8].

No account flag: RD-6 requires a prior upheld route dispute within 90 days, and the driver's profile shows 0 upheld [F18]; profile facts cannot decide the case anyway [RD-6].

segment_findings.reason: Rider message at 12:21, before the segment started at 12:25, named the place: 'Can you stop at Paya Lebar Square?' [F9], and the driver accepted [F10]; the car stopped there (4 min 0 s, not a pickup/drop-off point) [F2], confirmed by the driver [F12]. Under RD-3(a) the rider named the place and the car stopped there, so the segment driven to reach it is not a detour and its extra km are exempt in full [RD-3]. This segment is therefore not part of the refundable amount [RD-2]; the remaining ~0.51 km of billed excess [F1][F5] falls outside any measured segment and is not refunded under RD-2.

Keep following the most direct route where the rider hasn't asked otherwise.

Three kinds of agreement: (1) GENERAL route choice ('take whichever way is faster') covers a route chosen to get there, not an errand of the driver's own (a stop away from the route, a loop that reaches nothing: counts). (2) A SPECIFIC named road or area ('go round via X') covers driving on X only: the record must tie this segment to X (a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, a road name in a fact); timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path — if nothing ties them, the finding is undetermined (G13); if the record places this segment somewhere else (a stop away from X, the driver's own statement naming another road or place, a stop the driver chose the location of), the agreement to X does not cover it: counts. (3) Scope unclear: undetermined. A driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent (G11); a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment: counts. This finding changes the amount. Evidence — F9: Chat #1 12:21 rider: “Can you stop at Paya Lebar Square? I need to grab a parcel, 3-4 minutes.”; F10: Chat #2 12:21 driver: “Ok can”; F12: Driver statement (written after the trip, not part of the chat): “The rider asked me to stop at Paya Lebar Square, so I drove there and waited while the rider went in.” (F9, F10, F12)
